items.title: Elements lifting a basis of the conormal space of a regular ideal generate a regular sequence locally
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a sheaf of ideals on a locally ringed space which is quasi-regular, H1-regular or Koszul-regular, any elements of the stalk at a point lifting a basis of the conormal space extend, after shrinking, to a sequence of the corresponding type generating the ideal (statement lines 4716-4734). The counted proof is short but complete: it compares the given elements with a local generator, uses that quasi-regularity makes the conormal sheaf free of the right rank so that the two families have the same length, inverts the change-of-basis matrix on a neighbourhood because it is invertible modulo the maximal ideal at the point, and then transfers the stronger regularity notions through the isomorphism of Koszul complexes induced by that invertible matrix (proof lines 4736-4767). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard facts about regular sequences and their Koszul complexes.
